Nawal Al-Maghafi
Senior International Correspondent


Image source, EPA

Image caption, Houthi fighters during a protest against Saudi Arabia in Yemen's capital Sanaa on 17 July

The Houthis are often described simply as an Iranian proxy. The reality is more complicated.

There is no question that Iran has played a significant role in building the group’s military capabilities.

Over many years, Tehran has provided weapons, technology, training, and expertise that have helped transform the Houthis from a Yemeni insurgent movement into a force capable of firing sophisticated missiles and drones hundreds of miles beyond Yemen’s borders.

But that does not necessarily mean Tehran dictates every Houthi decision.

The Houthis have their own leadership, their own domestic ambitions inside Yemen and have demonstrated a degree of independence from Iran that distinguishes them from some other groups within Tehran’s so-called "Axis of Resistance".

What is particularly significant now is how closely their interests appear to be converging.

Iran has publicly backed the Houthis during the latest fighting. The geography helps explain why.

Iran already has the ability to exert enormous pressure on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The Houthis' advance towards Bab al-Mandab potentially creates pressure at another vital shipping route on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula.

That doesn’t mean the Houthis are simply taking orders from Tehran.

But at this moment, their military objectives inside Yemen and Iran’s interests in the wider regional war appear increasingly aligned.


Jack Grey
Live reporter


Fighters from the Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen have "taken control" of Perim Island in the Red Sea, a government source says.

The island divides the Bab al-Mandab Strait - a key global shipping route.

The strait, at the southern tip of the Red Sea, links both Europe - through the Suez Canal - and Saudi Arabia's western ports to the Indian Ocean and Asia as a whole.

Here are they key points:


In a statement on Friday, the Iran-backed group said "maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels" which it says are "subject to a blockade"

The Houthis claim to have made major advances in Yemen, after the group reportedly seized the red Sea port city of Mokha on Thursday

The group also claims it has expelled "Saudi-backed forces" from Yemen's western coast - but does not mention Perim Island

The Bab al-Mandab Strait has been a key shipping route for Saudi Arabia due to disruption to the Strait of Hormuz in the US-Iran war

Simi Jolaoso
BBC Africa correspondent


On the opposite side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait from Yemen lies tiny Djibouti, whose location has made it one of the most strategically important countries in Africa.

The narrow waterway between the African coast and Yemen connects the Gulf of Aden to the Red Sea and, beyond it, the Suez Canal, making it a crucial route for ships travelling between Europe and Asia.

That would explain the unusual concentration of military power along Djibouti's coastline.

The United States, China, France, Japan and Italy all operate military facilities there.

The US base at Camp Lemonnier supports around 4,000 US and allied personnel, while China opened its first overseas military support base in Djibouti in 2017. Both bases are only a few miles apart.

Japan's only overseas Self-Defense Force Base is also there; alongside long-established French forces and an Italian military base.

Their missions range from counter-piracy and counter-terrorism to protecting shipping, gathering intelligence and providing logistical support.

The location has taken on renewed importance as fighting intensifies just across the water.

Iran-backed Houthi forces are reported to have captured territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Several of the world's biggest military powers already have forces positioned beside this crucial shipping route.

So while much of the attention is currently on Yemen, the African shore illustrates just how much is at stake.


Nawal Al-Maghafi
Senior International Correspondent


The speed of the Houthi advance along Yemen's western coast
has taken many by surprise.

On Thursday, the group seized Mokha, the strategically
important Red Sea port that had been controlled by forces aligned with Yemen’s
internationally recognised government.

Contacts I have been speaking to in and around Mokha
described government forces pulling out rapidly as the Houthis entered.
Residents spoke of shops closing and families leaving the city, uncertain about
how far the group intended to advance. The UN says more than 46,000 people have
now fled amid the latest fighting.

But the Houthis have not stopped at Mokha.

On Friday, officials told the Associated Press that Houthi
forces had captured Perim, also known as Mayyun, a small but strategically
important island sitting directly inside the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi Arabia
has responded by striking Mokha airport.

That changes the strategic picture considerably.

Image source, EPA/Shutterstock

Image caption, The Houthis escalated fighting last week and have now reportedly taken over a strategic island in the Red Sea

Bab al-Mandab is the narrow gateway between the Red Sea and
the Gulf of Aden, and it's one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

On the other side of the Arabian Peninsula, shipping through
the Strait of Hormuz has already been severely disrupted by the war with Iran.
Saudi Arabia has therefore become increasingly dependent on its Red Sea route
to export oil.

The Houthis insist international shipping remains safe and
say their blockade is directed specifically at Saudi vessels. But their advance
gives them a much stronger position from which to threaten that shipping if
they choose to.

And that appears to be what is causing such alarm in Riyadh:
a conflict that had largely been frozen since 2022 has suddenly reached one of
the most strategically important waterways in the world.

The Houthis say their "large-scale" military operation against "Saudi-backed forces" in Yemen has achieved four key results.

They group's military spokesman claims:


The expulsion of "Saudi
enemy" troops from six districts in the Taiz
and Hodeidah regions

The targeting of "seven military divisions of the Saudi enemy's forces" and the "killing, capture, and wounding" of hundreds

The freeing of a number or prisoners "held
by the Saudi enemy's mercenaries for years"

The shooting down of nine aircraft across 32 operations to "intercept
Saudi warplanes"


We are yet to hear from Saudi Arabia on these latest developments.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea declares a
"large-scale" military operation launched on 3 September to expel
"Saudi-backed forces" from the western coast of Yemen to be a "success".

Sarea says in a statement the operation was launched due to Saudi Arabia's
"blatant aggression" against "our dear people".

He reiterates that "maritime navigation is safe for all
companies except for Saudi vessels" which it says are "subject to a
blockade".

The statement appears to make no mention of Perim Island, in the Bab
al-Mandab Strait.

We've just received an expected update from the Houthi's military spokesman.

It doesn't appear to mention the events that have unfolded over the past couple of days - we'll bring you a fuller look at the statement in just a moment.


Paul Adams
Diplomatic correspondent


The Houthis' lightning advance across the southern reaches
of the Tihama – Yemen's arid coastal plain – appears to have taken most
observers by surprise.

Until recently, the anti-Houthi coalition, known as the
National Resistance, held significant territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast. In
a matter of days, much of this has fallen to the Houthis, who are enjoying
their most significant battlefield gains for years.

But Hisham al-Omeisi, a Washington-based analyst at the
European Institute of Peace, says the latest developments are far from
surprising.

"The National Resistance forces have been warning… for
a while," he tells BBC News, "and unfortunately the international
community has been dragging its feet."

"Now that they are there [in Mokha, the Red Sea port
city], they're going to be entrenched and it’s going to be a lot more costly to
push them out.”

Some see the sudden collapse as an inevitable consequence of
a lack of coordination and sporadic infighting among anti-Houthi forces, as
well as deep divisions between Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, who
once formed the backbone of the international coalition supporting Yemen's
internationally-recognised government.

The US is in "regular communication" with regional
allies regarding Yemen and "remains focussed" on its
"counterterrorism goals against the Houthis", a US State Department
spokesperson tells the BBC.

"The United States' core interests in the Middle East
include ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and the region, as well
as preventing the export of terrorism," the statement reads.

It adds that the Trump administration has "clearly
demonstrated its commitment to defending these interests against aggression
from Iran and its proxies".

The State Department did not comment specifically on
the latest
advance of the Iran-backed Houthis against key Yemeni port sites on
the Red Sea.


Paul Adams
Diplomatic correspondent


The latest Houthi advances in Yemen's remote southwest don't
just represent a significant development in the course of Yemen's long civil
war but also threaten one of the world's most important maritime waterways.

By capturing the small southern port of Mocha and reportedly
occupying strategic islands in the southern Red Sea, the Houthis appear to be
in a position to control the flow of shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab
strait.

The Iranian-backed rebels, who control much of Yemen's
north, including the capital Sanaa, say they will only target Saudi-linked
ships, but their record in attacking a wide range of international vessels in
response to Israel's war in Gaza will make all nations using the Red Sea
extremely nervous.

To the north, satellite
images suggesting that Houthi missiles and drones struck Saudi Arabia’s
East-West pipeline – a vital alternative route for Saudi oil exports
following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year – points to an
effort by Iran’s Yemeni allies to add to the economic pressures generated by
the US-Israeli war with Iran.

With the Strait of Hormuz still mostly closed, the
possibility that the Bab al-Mandab might experience a similar fate is a real
worry.

By Shruti Menon, Thomas Spencer and Peter Mwai

BBC Verify has been examining material which shows fighters inside the key Red Sea port city of Mokha yesterday after it was captured by the Houthis.

One verified image shared on Telegram shows four armed men outside the Mohka airport terminal building, which is on the coast, just south of the main sea port.

Image source, Telegram

One video also shows armed men driving along one of the main roads in the centre of Mokha on four pick-up trucks.

In the clip, a man can be heard shouting a well-known Houthi slogan.

Image source, X

Houthi rebels have "taken control" of Perim Island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, according to a source. Earlier, we were reporting that the group had reached the key island.

The AFP news agency also says Houthis have "taken over" Perim Island, also referred to as Mayyun, according to eyewitnesses and a local government official.

"Boats carrying armed Houthi fighters reached Mayyun Island after government forces withdrew from it yesterday," the official tells AFP.


Jonathan Josephs
BBC business reporter


These latest escalations are likely to further squeeze global energy supplies in a week where the price of oil has already surged past $100 a barrel.

It’s the first time that has happened since late July, and that reflects traders concerns that Saudi Arabian oil supplies have fallen sharply.

With the world's second biggest oil producer under renewed attack from the Houthis there could be yet more pressure on those supplies.

Different figures for Saudi oil production have been published by in the last 24 hours but both show a big drop in August compared to July.

The International Energy Agency says it fell from 8.24 million, external barrels per day (bpd) to 5.97 million bpd, whereas Saudi government figures published by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) suggest the drop was from 8.14 million, external bpd to 6.24 million bpd.

Either way, the reduction is significant and it means production is heavily down on the same time last year.

Meanwhile, supplies via the Strait of Hormuz also remain reduced and President Trump’s suggestion that the US Iran conflict won't be over for some time means there is little prospect of that changing.

These higher energy prices continue to stoke inflation around the world which is putting pressure on central banks to increase interest rates as the European Central Bank did yesterday.

The chances of the US and Japan following suit next week are growing and the fear is that will weigh down economic growth.

By Paul Brown

Satellite imagery indicates there were several fires yesterday along a 68 mile (109km) stretch of Saudi Arabia's Abqaiq-Yanbu oil pipeline, which connects the Gulf and Red Sea.

European Space Agency imagery examined by BBC Verify shows a large plume of black smoke emanating from the vicinity of pumping station about 45 miles (72km) south of Medina.

Image source, Sentinel-3, Copernicus

Data from Nasa's fire-detection software FIRMS also show heat anomalies at eight points along the pipeline at around 17:00 BST yesterday.

One of these heat signatures is located at the same pumping station.

Image source, Nasa FIRMS

The pipeline is used by Saudi Arabia as an alternative to exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, which has been severely disrupted since the outbreak of the US-Israel war with Iran in February.

It is not possible to say what the exact cause of the smoke plume was, or how much damage has been caused, from the satellite images.

But experts on social media say, in the event of damage to a pipeline, safety systems are in place to close valves and redirect the pipeline's contents within a damaged section to burn off as flares to reduce further impact.

This could mean the multiple heat signatures are the result of these safety measures triggered by a single point of damage.

Following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz for
large periods of the US-Iran war, Saudi Arabia turned to its east-west pipeline
to transport oil exports to the Red Sea.

Earlier this year Saudi Arabia was diverting as much at 70%
of its crude exports from the Gulf to its Red Sea port of Yanbu through the
pipeline.

Through this pipeline, the Saudis have been able to ship oil
to Asia travelling south through the Red Sea's Bab al-Mandab Strait.

However, with the Houthis reportedly
reaching Perim Island, that divides the strait, Saudi oil exports could be impacted.

The Houthis say they pose no threat to international
shipping, except for vessels from Saudi Arabia.


Katy Watson
Reporting from Jerusalem


Yemen has been locked in a civil war since 2014 when the Houthi
movement, which has links with Iran, took the capital Sanaa.

It’s caused one of the worst humanitarian crises in the
world – thousands have died and nearly five million have been displaced, with
many facing starvation.

The roots of the conflict started in the Arab Spring of 2011 – an uprising forced the country's long-time authoritarian president, Ali
Abdullah Saleh, to hand over power to his deputy, Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi.

But the political transition was anything but smooth and the
Houthis took advantage of Hadi’s weakness and toppled his government

In March 2015, Saudi Arabia led air strikes against the
Houthis, intending to restore Hadi to power.

The Saudi-led coalition was worried that the Houthis' influence would empower their rival regional power Iran, in Yemen.

By 2022, a UN-brokered ceasefire was agreed – but it’s come
under huge strain this year with the war in Iran breaking out.

Peace has become fragile once again – the Houthis know they
will have leverage over the US if they can control the Red Sea

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea says a statement is expected - but does not provide more details about when.

In a post on Telegram, he says the group will announce "a large-scale, high-impact military operation".


Katy Watson
Reporting from Jerusalem


This reported move is significant – and would put the
Houthis in control of a key island that divides the Bab al-Mandab Strait in
two.

Perim sits at the narrowest point of the strait – in the
middle of a shipping lane that’s become increasingly important since the Iran
war began.

With the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz – a route
that accounts for a fifth of the world’s oil supply – Saudi Arabia has had to
reroute much of its oil through the East-West pipeline that connects to the Red
Sea.

Houthi officials say Red Sea navigation is safe for all
shipping companies except for Saudi vessels, pushing up the tension as well as
oil prices.

If the Houthis gain control of this waterway, that will put
Iran at an advantage and risks further reducing oil supplies which have risen
to above $100 a barrel.

The Bab al-Mandab Strait is the southern gateway to a key
shipping route that links Asia and Europe via the Red Sea and Suez canal.

Since the US and Israel's war effectively closed the Strait
of Hormuz in the Gulf, Saudi Arabia has relied on the Red Sea for oil exports.

The Saudis have been able to ship oil in bulk to customers
in Asia using tankers that depart south, past Yemen and the Bab al-Mandab
Strait, and out into the open Indian Ocean – but this is now at risk as the
Houthis threaten vessels passing by their coast.

The escalation of the conflict between the Houthis, Yemen's government
and Saudi Arabia has contributed to a surge in oil prices.

Image source, Getty Images

At least 46,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since
fighting escalated last week, the International Organization for Migration
(IOM) says.

In an update released today, the IOM adds the "number
is alarmingly rising by the hour".

"Families are being forced to flee for the second or third
time in this conflict, with almost nothing left," said Amy Pope, IOM Director
General.

TOP3大新闻


美司法部调查英伟达，涉及英伟达去年与人工智能芯片初创公司Groq达成的交易


据报道，美国司法部正在调查英伟达公司是否试图规避反垄断审查，这一调查涉及英伟达去年与人工智能芯片初创公司Groq达成的交易。去年12月，英伟达宣布与Groq达成一项价值170亿美元的交易。根据协议，英伟达获得Groq芯片技术的非排他性授权，同时吸纳了包括Groq创始人乔纳森·罗斯在内的部分高管。


美监管机构指出，这类“变相收购”行为会扼杀AI芯片行业的市场竞争，进一步强化英伟达在该领域的主导地位。路透社的报道指出，如果调查认定英伟达在交易操作方面存在问题，司法部可能对其处以罚款，但大概率不会要求撤销这笔交易。截至发稿，美国司法部、英伟达及Groq均未就这一报道置评。（央视财经）


罗永浩连用7个“抄的”吐槽苹果折叠屏iPhone Duo：我们究竟错过了多少科技创新带给我们的真正喜悦和幸福感


9月10日，罗永浩发文吐槽苹果折叠屏iPhone Duo：


还能说点实话吗？折叠机形态？抄的；屏下摄像头？抄的；矮胖的阔屏比例？抄的；侧面Dock？抄的；外屏/内屏无缝接力？抄的；多角度悬停？抄的；钛合金3D打印铰链盖？抄的；


折痕搞不定，所以不惜降低屏幕体验用雾面屏掩饰？这确实是原创的，但这又导致前摄在雾面屏下会糊，只好在雾面屏上单独磨亮前摄那一小块，导致本来要掩饰的前摄又被突出了？这确实是原创的，但这肯定是百分之百的屎上雕屎，相比之下，灵动岛也是自己拉，自己雕，但最后灵动岛毕竟还是雕出了一点花；好吧，折叠时的动画效果确实是原创的，而且效果很好看，所以拿了软文费的写手，和脑残果粉，只能拿着它反复高潮了。


最后……还有25天，就是老人家十五周年的忌日了，无限怀念和伤感。没法想象失去了他的这十多年，在一群笨蛋和笨蛋的抄袭者们的交替狂欢中，我们究竟错过了多少科技创新带给我们的真正喜悦和幸福感……（第一财经）


欧洲央行将三大关键利率上调25个基点


欧洲央行将存款机制利率上调25个基点至2.50%，将主要再融资利率上调25个基点至2.65%，将边际贷款利率上调25个基点至2.90%。（央视财经）


AI最前沿


DeepSeek V4.1 Flash模型正式发布


36氪获悉，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash模型正式发布。据介绍，该模型具备原生多模态视觉理解能力，新模型结构的设计初��是：能力上限更高、推理速度更快、吞吐更大、可扩展到更大参数模型。得益于模型架构的创新，DeepSeek下调了V4.1 Flash的定价。同时，为了更合理地调配资源，仍然采用峰谷定价，闲时价格为高峰时段价格的一半，鼓励用户根据实际使用情况调整任务时间。新价格于2026年9月10日12:00开始生效。


DeepSeek Harness更新：适配DeepSeek V4.1 Flash模型


36氪获悉，DeepSeek Harness v0.1.5版本现已发布。新版本与DeepSeek V4.1 Flash模型训练深度结合，模型在DeepSeek Harness的不同配置中都进行了专项训练和优化。同时，新版DeepSeek Harness为插件作者提供了更多标准化的UI扩展入口，新增了文件上传、侧边栏文件预览等功能，优化了UI的性能与交互，并持续增加与模型研究前沿深度结合的实验性功能。


宇树科技：完全开源UnifoLM-WLA-1.0具身基座模型


36氪获悉，宇树完全开源UnifoLM-WLA-1.0具身基座模型，单模型统筹桌面与全身移动操作，支持跨任务、跨末端执行器泛化。


Anthropic向欧盟开放Mythos模型访问权限


据报道，Anthropic已向欧盟网络安全机构开放其Mythos人工智能模型的访问权限。欧盟委员会发言人Thomas Regnier表示：“在与Anthropic进行建设性沟通后，我们可以确认，欧盟网络安全局（ENISA）已获准访问Mythos 5，目前正在测试。”Regnier称，ENISA将无法访问该模型的最新版本Mythos 5.1。（界面新闻）


大公司/大事件


《金融强国建设“十五五”规划》正式出台


中国人民银行副行长陆磊9月10日在国新办举行的“开局起步‘十五五’”系列主题新闻发布会上表示，近日，《金融强国建设“十五五”规划》正式出台。为实施好相关部署，中国人民银行制定印发了《中国人民银行“十五五”改革发展规划》，配套出台了9份相关领域的行动方案。（新华社）


298项重要国家标准发布，涉及AI、半导体等


9月10日了解到，国家标准委批准发布298项重要国家标准。其中，强制性国家标准27项，推荐性国家标准271项，涉及高新技术、传统产业、安全生产、农业等领域。该批标准发布后将在推动产业高质量发展、提升人民群众生活品质、保障生命财产安全等方面发挥重要作用。在高新技术方面，发布人工智能、智能语音交互、智慧服务等47项国家标准，将在电力、港口、石油、家居等领域规范AI发展，赋能行业提质增效。发布半导体器件、集成电路等26项国家标准，规范半导体产业发展，强化产业链韧性，助力科技自立自强。（央视新闻）


证监会李超：努力将A股打造为境内优质企业上市首选地


在国新办新闻发布会上，证监会副主席李超表示，下一步，证监会将实施更具包容性的发行上市、并购重组等制度，努力将A股打造为境内优质企业上市首选地。动态完善上市标准体系，有序扩大向新向优的覆盖面。加快修订再融资注册办法等制度规则。促进北交所、新三板一体化高质量发展。进一步畅通私募创投基金“募投管退”循环，引导投早、投小、投长期、投硬科技。（证券时报）


印度政府机构建议对小米公司展开调查，外交部回应


外交部发言人郭嘉昆主持例行记者会。路透社提问，印度公司事务部下属的严重欺诈调查局（SFIO）建议对小米公司展开调查，理由是小米公司在商业模式及遵守外商投资法规方面涉嫌违规。请问外交部对此有何评论？郭嘉昆表示，“我不了解你提到的具体情况。中印经贸合作本质上是互利共赢的，希望印方为各国企业在印投资经营提供公平、公正、透明、非歧视的营商环境。”（澎湃新闻）


美股三大指数集体收跌，苹果涨超3%


36氪获悉，9月10日收盘，美股三大指数集体下跌，道指跌0.6%，纳指跌0.65%，标普500指数跌0.58%。大型科技股多数下跌，英特尔、甲骨文跌超5%，英伟达跌超2%，Meta、特斯拉跌超1%，亚马逊、奈飞小幅下跌；苹果涨超3%，谷歌、微软小幅上涨。热门中概股跌多涨少，蔚来跌超3%，哔哩哔哩、富途控股、老虎证券、理想汽车、小鹏集团跌超2%，百度跌超1%；爱奇艺、腾讯音乐、京东小幅上涨。


传月之暗面拟赴香港、上海双重上市，知情人士：消息不实


有报道称，国内头部大模型企业月之暗面正考虑在香港和上海两地上市，以借此获得更多资金。对此，知情人士称，该消息不实。（财联社）


燧原科技：股票今日在科创板上市


9月9日燧原科技发布公告，公司股票于2026年9月11日在上海证券交易所科创板上市；截至公告披露日（9月9日），公司尚未盈利，自上市之日起纳入科创成长层。本次发行后总股本为4.3亿股，上市初期无限售流通股数量为1790.03万股，占本次发行后总股本的比例为4.1595%。(金十数据)


2026年A股上市公司现金分红榜单揭晓，2.4万亿元“真金白银”落地


中国上市公司协会9月10日发布2026年上市公司现金分红榜单。数据显示，2025财务年度A股上市公司分红总额高达2.4万亿元，同比增长3.3%，创下历史新高。近七成上市公司派发“真金白银”，现金分红已从阶段性热潮全面迈入“常态化”新阶段。（上证报）


寒武纪回应AI处理器大幅调价传闻


有消息称，包括寒武纪在内的中国AI芯片厂商大幅上调现有及新一代AI处理器的售价。其中，寒武纪对其下一代暂定命名为690的芯片重新定价，较两个月前的参考报价上涨20%至30%。对此，记者以投资者身份致电寒武纪，公司接线工作人员表示，公司并未发布涨价相关消息，请投资者以公司在官方指定信息披露媒体披露的相关公告为准，切勿轻信市场上的相关传闻。公司无法对产品后续价格走势作出判断。（21财经）


月之暗面官宣企业合作伙伴“登月计划”，首批签约多家上市公司


36氪获悉，9月10日，月之暗面正式启动Kimi企业合作伙伴“登月计划”，将以FDE模型与各行业系统集成商共建前置部署工程师队伍，深入客户现场，推动大模型进入企业核心业务流程。这也是国内首家采用FDE模型进行AI末端部署的大模型公司。首批签约伙伴包括中软国际、金山云、华胜天成、亚康股份、亚信科技等，覆盖软件信息服务、通信、基础设施、云计算等领域。该计划将持续面向IT服务商、软件服务商及咨询机构开放。


央行：将在9月14日至9月17日开展隔夜逆回购操作，每日操作量不超过6000亿元


36氪获悉，央行发布公告，为更好匹配银行体系短期流动性需求，中国人民银行将在9月14日至9月17日开展隔夜逆回购操作，采用固定利率、数量招标，每日操作量不超过6000亿元。


机构：预估2026年苹果iPhone Duo出货量约500万支，市占近25%


36氪获悉，TrendForce集邦咨询估计，2026年苹果首款折叠手机iPhone Duo出货量约500万支，将可助力苹果在折叠手机市场取得约24.8%市占率。该机构预估，2026年全球折叠手机出货量约2020万支，较2025年微幅成长0.5%。若排除苹果的贡献，2026年安卓品牌合计出货量仅约1520万支，年减逾20%，主因是零部件成本大幅度上涨，各品牌出货多持平前一年或出现下降。在此情况下，预估三星出货量约710万支，市占率35.1%；华为出货量约500万支，市占率24.8%。


苹果iPhone Duo遭黄牛爆炒，首发代抢标价9.9万元


9月10日，苹果首款折叠屏手机iPhone Duo发布后，经查询闲鱼等二手交易平台发现，已有多名商家上线iPhone Duo首发代抢服务，有黄牛标价高达9.9万元。经询问多位商家发现，iPhone Duo加价普遍已炒至5000元左右，最低加价也在1000元以上，目前黄牛端1TB、2TB版的行情价仍在上调，不少黄牛以“第一天拿到现货”招揽买家，部分消费者预约抢购的定金已炒至800元左右，“跑单不退”。（第一财经）


字节跳动聘请前Coatue高管，加码AI领域投资交易


据报道，字节跳动有限公司聘请了Coatue Management的前高管掌管企业投资团队。据知情人士透露，Jiang Kai担任位于香港的财务投资部门负责人，向首席财务官高准（Julie Gao）汇报。知情人士表示，此次任命将帮助字节跳动建立一套更为系统化的机制，投资新兴科技初创企业。（新浪财经）


国办：推动龙头企业率先践行“60日付现承诺”


36氪获悉，国务院办公厅印发《关于加强中小企业回款难问题治理有关工作的通知》。其中提出，推动龙头企业率先践行“60日付现承诺”。发布行业领域大型企业及时支付倡议，引导大型企业特别是龙头企业带头发布并践行自货物、工程、服务交付之日起60日内以现金方式向中小企业支付账款的承诺。督促大型企业严格按照企业会计准则记账，纠正不签合同、不开发票、不确认债权债务关系等行为。指导相关协会开展及时支付自律管理，制定及时支付自律规范。


香港证监会因涉嫌操纵首次公开招股行为而暂停拨康视云股份交易


36氪获悉，香港证监会发布公告，指示港交所自2026年9月10日上午9时正起，暂停拨康视云-B的股份交易。证监会对拨康视云的首次公开招股可能曾被人为操纵，以营造对拨康视云股份需求的假象表示严重关注。由于调查仍在进行中，证监会不会作进一步评论。


苹果回应下架iPhone 17 Pro


9月10日苹果秋季发布会后，在苹果官网检索发现，iPhone品类目前仅有iPhone Air、iPhone 17、iPhone 17e、iPhone 16在售，iPhone 17 Pro系列已下架。对此，苹果官方客服表示，发布新产品时，iPhone 17 Pro系列会下架，只留基础款在售。上述客服明确表示，“不会重新上架”。（中新经纬）


白宫高官称美伊战事或持续至特朗普任期结束


据美国《华尔街日报》9日报道，白宫高级官员私下向美国总统特朗普指出，美伊战事可能会持续至其总统任期结束。报道援引多名美官员的话说，在白宫椭圆形办公室和战情室举行的会议中，美国副总统万斯、国务卿鲁比奥等人与特朗普讨论了伊朗可能在美国的封锁和其他军事压力下继续抵抗的情况，这或许会造成冲突持续至2029年1月的总统就职日之后。报道还说，白宫高级官员私下承认这场军事冲突可能会拖上数年，这与特朗普声称美国已击败伊朗军队、伊朗政权即将投降的说法相矛盾。（新华社）


存储巨头铠侠CEO：价格已涨得够高


9月9日，今年4月份刚接任铠侠（Kioxia）CEO的太田裕雄（Hiroo Ota）直言，“（存储）价格已经涨得够高了！”他表示，已指示业务团队不要向数据中心客户大幅提高报价，以免打击AI产业的投资意愿。太田强调，即便是超大规模数据中心运营商，其预算也是有限的，若价格继续失控上涨，最终将反噬AI投资意愿，进而冲击整体内存市场的长期成长。


铠侠的核心产品是NAND闪存及固态硬盘（SSD），与前三个月相比，铠侠6月份的NAND闪存平均价格上涨了70%，而前一个季度的价格涨幅超过一倍。分析师预计，该公司截至3月份的财年营业利润将增长九倍以上。（财联社）


功率半导体大厂瑞萨电子宣布涨价


功率大厂瑞萨电子宣布对产品价格体系进行调整，新价格将于2027年1月1日起正式生效。今年3月，该厂也曾发布涨价通知，并于今年7月1日生效。瑞萨在此次通知中提到，目前行业仍面临原材料、能源、先进封装、制造产能以及全球物流等方面的结构性成本上涨。


功率半导体是电能转换与电路控制的核心器件，广泛应用于电力电子领域，近年来AI数据中心建设带来电源控制和机柜供电相关功率芯片需求激增。据《科创板日报》不完全统计，除瑞萨电子外，2026年以来已有多家功率半导体厂商宣布涨价，涨价经历好几轮，涵盖海外龙头与国内主要厂商。（财联社）


台积电1.4纳米建厂加速，明年下半年有望量产


据报道，台积电中科扩建二期1.4纳米建厂全面加速，第一座（P1）厂目前已完成钢构结构体，预计明年4月即可试机，明年下半年有望量产。报道称，台积电已提出申请，在基地建置两座临时办公室，预计明年4月同步完工，首批将有超5400名营运及外包人员进驻。这也代表P1厂将在明年4月启动试机，下半年就有机会量产，较原订2028年量产进度提前许多。（界面新闻）


OpenAI呼吁美国制定强制性全国AI安全规则，并支持四项加州法案


OpenAI当地时间9月9日表示，将推动美国建立具有强制约束力、按照模型能力和风险分级的全国人工智能安全制度。公司提出，针对开发最先进模型的少数大型实验室，应设置统一的测试、独立评估、网络安全和重大事故报告要求。与此同时，OpenAI正式支持四项已经通过加州议会的人工智能法案。公司称，其中部分法案此前未获其支持，此次调整立场源于近期模型能力快速提升。（新浪财经）


英伟达CEO黄仁勋称网络安全将成AI下一个重大市场


英伟达联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋表示，网络安全将成为人工智能（AI）的下一个重大市场，AI技术的发展势将颠覆这个以保护计算机系统为主要任务的行业。“网络安全很可能会成为AI下一个主要应用场景，”黄仁勋周四在旧金山举行的高盛科技会议上对与会者表示。黄仁勋表示，AI模型实现计算机编程自动化，正给网络安全行业带来冲击，因为代码遭利用的速度越来越快，修复也须随之加快。（新浪财经）


OpenAI限制Adobe及其他竞争对手在ChatGPT投放广告


OpenAI已告知部分商业合作伙伴，将不再接受图像及音频生成类产品在ChatGPT内投放广告，这类产品与OpenAI自身功能构成竞争关系。这项调整此前未有相关报道，也尚未更新至其官方广告政策页面，此举令Adobe等销售同类产品的现有广告商猝不及防。倘若该政策进一步扩大适用到其他竞品，新规则或将压缩OpenAI潜在的广告收入空间。（新浪财经）


上市进行时


汉盛海装北交所IPO过会


36氪获悉，北交所上市委员会召开2026年第84次审议会议。审议结果显示，汉盛（上海）海洋装备技术股份有限公司符合发行条件、上市条件和信息披露要求。


大公司财报


合富中国：2026年1-8月合并营收4.38亿元，同比下降9.84%


36氪获悉，合富中国公告，2026年1-8月累计合并营业收入为人民币4.38亿元，较2025年同期的4.86亿元下降9.84%；相较2024年同期降幅21.93%，年降幅收窄12.09%。上述数据未经会计师事务所审计或审阅。


台积电8月销售额5148亿元台币，同比增长53.3％


台积电8月销售额5148亿元台币，同比增长53.3％；1-8月累计销售额3.39万亿元台币，同比增长39.3％。（界面新闻）


甲骨文第一财季调整后营收为193.5亿美元，超市场预期


甲骨文第一财季调整后营收为193.5亿美元，市场预估为191.3亿美元；第一财季软件营收55.5亿美元，市场预期56.7亿美元；第一财季云基础设施（IAAS）营收73.9亿美元，市场预估71.9亿；预计财年调整后每股收益8.10美元；预计第二财季总营收增长30%至34%；第一财季云应用(SAAS)营收42.2亿美元，市场预估为42.6亿美元。（财联社）


江南布衣：2026财年收入同比增9%至60.46亿元


36氪获悉，江南布衣公布截至2026年6月30日止年度业绩，江南布衣全年收入60.46亿元，同比增长9.0%；净利润9.97亿元，同比增长11.1%；毛利率同比提高1个百分点至66.6%。其中，线上收入增长20.5%至14.48亿元，线下收入增长5.8%至45.98亿元。


投融资


“云通数达”完成4000万元B轮融资，深耕AI交通信号控制新赛道


近日，AI智慧交通企业云通数达完成4000万元B轮融资。本轮由温州湾投资、金昌投资、海纳汇聚作为新股东参投，每日互动、华旦资本等老股东继续加码。资金将用于数智绿波、车路云一体化产品迭代，推进AI信控智能体场景落地，加速技术迭代与海外市场拓展。目前数智绿波已落地国内近40个城区，落地绿波道路近900条，同时业务积极布局一带一路国家市场。


“镭昱半导体”完成近亿元Pre-A4轮融资


36氪获悉，近日，“镭昱半导体”（Raysolve）宣布完成近亿元Pre-A4轮融资，本轮融资由招银国际资本领投，沣途资本、某产业方跟投，木雁资本担任独家财务顾问。所融资金将主要用于技术与产品迭代、应用验证及产业合作，进一步推动镭昱在近眼显示与光互联领域的产业化进程。


马斯克旗下Boring Company完成30亿美元D轮融资，估值达230亿美元


据公司声明显示，马斯克旗下The Boring Company完成30亿美元D轮融资，估值达230亿美元。本轮融资由阿联酋及关联投资实体领投。本次投资将用于在阿联酋境内大规模落地地下基建项目，其中包含总长超150公里的隧道网络。本轮其他核心投资方还包括Human Capital、Vy Capital、Valor Equity Partners、红杉资本、a16z、淡马锡、Shamal Holding以及Baron Capital，同时也有大量新老投资者参与跟投。本次达成的合作协议，是在此前已中标迪拜Loop项目基础上的进一步拓展。（财联社）


“星语智能”完成千万级天使轮融资

“大鱼智行”完成近亿元Pre-B轮融资


36氪获悉，智能轻出行企业“大鱼智行”近期完成近亿元Pre-B轮融资，本轮由同鑫资本领投，多家机构跟投。融资资金将主要用于新品研发、智能化技术升级、全球品牌建设及供应链能力提升。

小米18 Fold 9月10日开售


36氪获悉，小米18 Fold 9月10日率先开售，作为小米首款起售价过万旗舰，小米18 Fold搭载小米玄戒O3旗舰处理器、小米澎湃OS4人车家全生态操作系统、全球首发国产长鑫LPDDR6内存等亮点技术功能，较自家上代折叠屏产品销量提升300%。


千问新款AI眼镜首次曝光，或加入虹膜支付能力


36氪获悉，9月10日，千问新款AI眼镜疑似现身2026年外滩大会AI支付展区，该款眼镜被黑色遮蔽材料大面积包裹，暂时无法判断更多功能及硬件细节；但从展区内容来看，新品或将首次引入虹膜识别能力，通过更精准的身份匹配，进一步提升AI眼镜支付的安全性与交互便捷度。

items.title: 派早报：商务部回应美国 AI 蒸馏指控
items.author: 少数派编辑部
items.summary:
9 月 9 日，商务部官网发布新闻稿，介绍商务部新闻发言人就美发布中国人工智能企业对美蒸馏活动相关网络安全公告答记者问的情况。

该问答指出，注意到美东时间 9 月 8
items.text:
9 月 9 日，商务部官网发布新闻稿，介绍商务部新闻发言人就美发布中国人工智能企业对美蒸馏活动相关网络安全公告答记者问的情况。

该问答指出，注意到美东时间 9 月 8 日，美国家安全局、网络安全与基础设施安全局、联邦调查局联合发布公告，指责中国人工智能企业对美开展「工业规模」蒸馏，获取美前沿模型能力，并向美企提出相关防御措施建议。

商务部表示，美方指控于事无凭，于法无据，是将蒸馏这一业内正常的技术和商业问题政治化、工具化，并在实践中搞双重标准。美方相关公告，是其在人工智能领域推行科技霸权、搞算力垄断，打压竞争的又一明证。中方对此坚决反对。

新闻发言人还说，蒸馏是人工智能领域各个模型间互相学习的通行做法，本质是中性技术手段，包括美企在内的全球模型企业都在用。多次单方面指责中国企业从事「工业规模」蒸馏，将行业通行做法抹黑为攻击行为，既反映了美方的焦虑，又体现了双重标准。

商务部表示，注意到美个别人工智能企业滥用竞争优势地位，在用户协议中设置宽泛的地域限制等霸王条款。美方相关蒸馏指控，有为这些霸王条款背书之嫌。如果美方以打击蒸馏为名，实施遏压中国人工智能企业的行动，中方必将坚决采取措施予以反制。希望美方与中方相向而行，通过对话和沟通管控风险，推动人工智能产业惠及全球。

据 Engadgets 报道，为规避欧盟的反垄断巨额罚款，Google 近日宣布将对其在欧盟境内的搜索引擎展示方式进行重大调整。此前，欧盟委员会指控 Google 滥用搜索领域的市场主导地位、在检索结果中偏袒自家业务，并对其开出 4.6 亿欧元的罚单；若不配合整改，Google 还将面临更高金额的处罚风险。

根据整改方案，欧洲用户在检索旅游、出行及餐饮等内容时，Google 将在页面顶部优先突出展示第三方垂直比价与聚合平台（如 Expedia、Hotels.com 等），随后附带展示另外两家平台。与此同时，Google 原先置顶的酒店、航班与餐厅轮播展示栏将下移，实时比价等信息也将不再展示。展示排名的具体顺序仍由 Google 算法决定。

该措施旨在满足欧盟于 2024 年实施的《数字市场法》（DMA）。作为欧盟规范大型科技平台的核心监管法规，该法明确禁止具备「守门人」地位的企业在排序中给予自身服务优于第三方竞争对手的待遇。欧盟此前已责令 Google 在 60 天内完成整改，但 Google 尚未公布新版界面正式面向欧洲公众上线的确切时间表。

对于被迫调整算法，Google 方面表示强烈不满。Google 知识与信息高级副总裁 Nick Fox 说，为满足 DMA 合规要求，公司不得不降低服务标准，这构成了 Google 搜索「历史上最大幅度的质量降级」。Google 还声称，此类改动剥离了用户日常依赖的功能，实际上是扶持了线上中介平台并牺牲了本地实体商户，此前类似的调整已导致欧洲本地商家获得的免费直接预订流量下滑了 30%。

9 月 9 日，苹果官方支持页面更新了《Apple 智能使用条款》及《了解 Apple 智能使用限制》等篇目。

苹果在上述支持文章中指出，部分 Apple 智能和 Siri AI 功能将在未来实施使用限制。如果在某个特定功能上达到使用限制，该功能将在一段时间后再次可用。使用限制可能因功能、请求复杂性、系统需求、系统策略和其他因素而异。要增加对此类功能的使用权限，需要付费。

根据支持文章，将受到使用限制的功能包括但不限于：Siri AI；智能照片编辑工具，包括消除、扩展和空间构图；图乐园；快捷指令中的 AFM 3 Cloud 和 AFM 3 Cloud Pro 模型；以及在专用云计算中使用 Apple 基础模型的开发者 App。

苹果没有说明付费细节，但曾在 WWDC 上表示 iCloud+ 方案将包括更多 Apple 智能用量。

此外，根据使用条款，苹果还会根据用量、频率、请求复杂性、系统需求和使用模式等因素，限制其认定为不合理使用的情形。

据路透社报道，9 月 9 日，OpenAI 韩国区总经理 Harrison Kim 在首尔举行的新闻发布会上表示，双方在联合研发与生产下一代芯片方面「取得了显著进展」。

OpenAI 正加速构建自研硬件生态。此前，为保障算力供应并降低对单一供应商的依赖，OpenAI 于今年 6 月公布了与博通联合设计的首款推理芯片 Jalapeno，交由台积电代工制造。三星电子与 SK 海力士也已就 OpenAI 的「星际之门」（Stargate）数据中心项目签署了内存供应意向书。

对此，三星电子发表声明称，无法对涉及客户的信息置评。

除芯片研发外，三星电子也是 ChatGPT 全球部署规模最大的企业客户之一，其韩国本土及海外的研发、营销与销售等部门已全面接入该工具。OpenAI 披露，截至 8 月底，韩国企业及机构的 ChatGPT 企业版用户数量同比激增约 28 倍，已成为美国本土以外最大的付费订阅市场。

9 月 10 日，微软宣布，著名游戏制作人小岛秀夫正在开发的全新动作谍战新作 PHYSINT，将改由 Xbox 负责全球发行。同时，小岛秀夫通过社交平台表示，小岛工作室于今年 6 月中旬意外收到索尼取消 PHYSINT 企划的通知。为了维持项目推进，团队在过去三个月内积极接洽各方，最终与 Xbox 达成愿景一致的新合作。

索尼 PlayStation 随后发表声明，证实经审慎考虑后决定终止该项目的合作开发，但表示双方长达三十年的合作关系依然稳固。PHYSINT 原为索尼阵营重点支持的重磅作品，最早于 2024 年索尼 State of Play 发布会上亮相，定位于融合交互游戏与电影叙事的次世代数字娱乐作品，被视为小岛经典代表作《合金装备》（Metal Gear Solid）的精神续作。小岛工作室表示，PHYSINT 目前仍在积极推进中，预计距离最终发售仍需数年时间。

Xbox 新任 CEO Asha Sharma 将深化与小岛的合作列为业务调整期的关键战略。除继续推进此前公布的恐怖游戏 OD 外，微软与小岛工作室的合作还将进一步拓展至影视领域。在发行排期上，OD 的面世时间将早于 PHYSINT。

9 月 10 日，DeepSeek 发布了 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 模型。这是 DeepSeek 新模型结构系列中的最小尺寸的模型，具备原生多模态视觉理解能力。

据介绍，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 为 552B 参数的 MoE 模型，采用了全新的 Causal-Encoder-Decoder 结构，输入和输出不对称，输入激活只有 8B，输出激活 16B，成本显著低于已知的同尺寸模型。同时，V4.1 Flash 还采用了新的预训练方式、经过了更大规模的强化学习后训练，在基准测试中，成功超越了包括 DeepSeek V4 Pro 在内的一众旗舰模型的智能水平。

DeepSeek 下调了 V4.1 Flash 的定价。空闲时段输入缓存命中为每百万 Token 价格 0.02 元、输入缓存未命中为每百万 Token 价格 1 元，输出为每百万 Token 价格 4 元；高峰时段各项价格均为上述空闲时段价格的两倍。

官方表示，V4.1 Flash 在性能、费用、速度、总用时等各项指标上已全面超越 V4 Pro，因此我们计划有序下线 V4 Pro 模型。北京时间 2026 年 9 月 14 日 12:00 之后，至未来 V4.1 Pro 上线之前，用户访问 V4 Pro 的请求将全部路由到 V4.1 Flash，并按 V4.1 Flash 单价计费。

items.title: NTSB issues investigative update on B-767 runway excursion accident in Miami
items.author: mckn1ght
items.summary: ​​WASHINGTON (Sept. 9, 2026) — The National Transportation Safety Board is providing the following update on its investigation into the Sept. 6 runway
items.text:
​​WASHINGTON (Sept. 9, 2026) — The National Transportation Safety Board is providing the following update on its investigation into the Sept. 6 runway excursion accident involving 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-33A cargo airplane, at Miami International Airport.


The following information from the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) and ﬂight data recorder (FDR) is preliminary and subject to change.


The NTSB recovered the CVR and FDR from the accident site and transported them to the NTSB’s Vehicle Recorder Laboratory in Washington, DC, where they were successfully read out.

The aircraft was equipped with an Acron Aviation (formerly L3Harris) model FA2100 CVR and an Ontic (formerly Honeywell) model SSFDR FDR.

The CVR contained more than 2 hours of good quality audio across four channels.

The FDR contained approximately 54 hours of data and recorded more than 400 parameters.

The NTSB will convene a CVR group in the near future at NTSB headquarters in Washington, DC, to review the accident ﬂight recording and produce a written transcript.

A summary of select events captured on the CVR during the ﬁnal few minutes of the recording is provided below. All times are referenced relative to the end of the CVR recording. The times and descriptions are preliminary and subject to change.


​06:02
​A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 1 degree.​


​04:18
​The ﬂight crew checked in with Miami tower and were cleared to
​land on runway 30.

​02:53
​​A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 5 degrees.


​02:37
​The ﬂight crew lowered the landing gear.​


​02:14
​A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 15 degrees.​


​01:42
​A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 20 degrees, and the other pilot cautioned they were too fast. The other pilot made additional comments regarding the aircraft’s excessive speed throughout the remainder of the recording. There was not a consistent verbal response to the comments about speed.

​01:23
​Sounds consistent with autopilot disconnect.​


01:12
​Electronic “one thousand” callout.


01:04
​Electronic “sink rate sink rate” callout.​


​00:58
​Electronic “ﬁve hundred” callout.​


​00:57
​Electronic “sink rate sink rate” callout.


​00:54
​Electronic “one hundred” callout.​


​00:50
​Electronic “minimums” callout.​


​00:48
​Electronic “too low terrain” callout. Annunciated four times.


​00:41
​​A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 30 degrees.


​00:40
​Electronic “forty” callout.​


​00:39
​Electronic “too low terrain” callout.


​00:36
​Electronic “ten” callout.​


​00:31
​Sounds similar to the aircraft touching down.


​00:15
​A pilot called for a go-around.​


​00:10
​Sounds similar to the aircraft departing the paved surface.


​00:00
​The CVR recording ended.​


A summary of select events captured on the FDR during the ﬁnal few minutes of the FDR recording is provided below. All times are referenced relative to the end of the FDR recording. Note that the CVR and FDR times have not been precisely synchronized. The times and descriptions are preliminary and subject to change.

​00:30
The nose and right main gear touched down at a groundspeed of 158 knots.


​00:23
​The brakes were applied at a groundspeed of 146 knots.


​00:19
​The left main gear touched down at a groundspeed of 134
knots.​


​00:15
​Brakes were released at a groundspeed of 120 knots and throttles were increased to a value consistent with go-around thrust.

​00:11
​The throttles were reduced to idle power and the brakes were re-applied. The groundspeed was 117 knots. The throttles remained at idle, and brakes remained applied until the end of the recording.

​00:07
​Recorded lateral, longitudinal, and vertical acceleration values
changed markedly; the FDR data indicated a groundspeed of 96 knots.

​00:00
​The FDR recording ended. The ﬁnal recorded groundspeed was 65 knots. There was no indication in the recorded data that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed.​


​Additional information, including video of media briefings, photos and other factual materials, is available on the
accident investigation webpage.

To report an incident/accident or if you are a public safety agency, please call 1-844-373-9922 or 202-314-6290 to speak to a Watch Officer at the NTSB Response Operations Center (ROC) in Washington, DC (24/7).

Las Vegas, in 2015, was arguably the biggest sports city in America without a major sports team. By 2028, there could be an NHL, NFL, WNBA and an NBA franchise all within the City of Sin.

So why the very sudden change of heart?

This is a story of how America's major sports once viewed Las Vegas as untouchable because they believed gambling and sporting integrity could not coexist. But now they see the two as “reinforcing” one another.

Today we're going completely off grid in Afghanistan — two hours from Kabul, deep into the mountains of Wardak, to my friend Bilal Kamal's home village, where he's taking me to meet the elders — his father and uncles — and cook a traditional Afghan feast together. We make stops along the way for melons and firewood, get a welcome I was not ready for, and then watch the entire preparation of a whole lamb plus a spread of countryside dishes, cooked exactly the way they've been made in this village for generations. Sitting down to share this meal with the elders was one of the most powerful food experiences of my life — this is traditional Afghan village food you will not see anywhere else!

Peptides are everywhere right now. I was at the gym talking to my buddy Jeff, who asked me what my “peptide stack” was. I’m like, “My peptide stack?” Neither one of us was actually taking peptides, but he’d heard so much about them that he was curious. And that’s exactly what’s happening right now. You open Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube, and somebody is talking about peptides, weight-loss drugs, recovery, anti-aging, muscle building, or some new biohack that’s supposedly going to change your life. There’s so much hype that I think we need to understand what peptides actually are before we start injecting random sh*t into our bodies.

The first thing you need to understand is that peptides aren’t magic—they’re messengers. Peptides are small chains of amino acids that essentially send instructions to your body. Think of them like text messages: regulate appetite, release growth hormone, repair tissue, or perform some other specific function. A peptide isn’t testosterone, and it isn’t a steroid. Different peptides send different messages, which means they can have different benefits and risks. The second thing you need to understand is that just because something is called a peptide doesn’t mean it’s safe. Everything you put into your body can potentially have risks and side effects. One of my biggest concerns is where people get this stuff. There are shady websites selling compounds as “research chemicals,” and you may have absolutely no idea whether what you’re buying is sterile, properly dosed, or even what the label claims it is. If you’re considering something like this, I believe you need legitimate medical oversight, appropriate testing, proper dosing, and ongoing monitoring—not some dude on the Internet promising you a shortcut. And that brings me to probably the most important point: peptides will not fix a bad lifestyle. Everybody wants the shortcut. We want to lose fat faster, recover quicker, look younger, build muscle, sleep better, and feel incredible. But a recovery peptide doesn’t replace sleep, and something designed to support performance doesn’t replace actually going to the gym. These things can potentially support a plan, but they cannot replace the fundamentals—exercise, nutrition, sleep, consistency, and taking care of your body.

Before I would ever consider taking a peptide, I’d ask myself:

What problem am I actually trying to solve? Don’t take something simply because your buddy is taking it.

Is there legitimate research showing that it actually works? TikTok testimonials aren’t scientific evidence.

Am I getting it through a legitimate medical provider? Where it comes from, how it’s administered, and how you’re monitored matter.

Do I understand the risks and potential side effects? There is no free lunch when it comes to this stuff.

Have I fixed the basics first? If your diet sucks, you don’t exercise, and you’re looking for a magic bullet, you’re probably wasting your time, money, and energy.

At the end of the day, I don’t think peptides are inherently good or bad. They’re tools. The right peptide, for the right person, for the right reason, with legitimate medical supervision, could potentially be incredibly effective. But don’t get sucked into the hype and start experimenting with your body because some jacked dude on social media told you it changed his life. Do your homework, understand the risks, fix the fundamentals, and if you decide to explore peptides, do it intelligently and under proper medical supervision.

I’ve always been paranoid about losing my hair because male pattern baldness absolutely runs rampant in my family. Both grandfathers, my uncles, my cousins—bald. So about five years ago, when I started noticing more hair in the drain, on my pillow, and in my brush, I freaked out. My hairline was changing, my widow’s peak was disappearing, and I was thinning around the crown. I knew I needed to do something.

I threw everything at it. I tried minoxidil, finasteride, and a red-light therapy cap. Unfortunately, minoxidil irritated my scalp and made my hair feel greasy, while finasteride caused sexual side effects almost immediately. That was a deal breaker for me. I stopped both, but I wasn’t about to stop looking for ways to protect my hair. The big thing I learned is that for a lot of guys, hair loss is connected to DHT, or dihydrotestosterone. DHT can attach to susceptible hair follicles and gradually cause them to miniaturize. The hairs become finer and weaker until eventually they stop growing. That’s why one of the most important lessons I can give you is this: don’t wait until your hair is gone to start caring about it. The earlier you notice thinning and take action, the better opportunity you have to preserve what you’ve got.

Because traditional treatments didn’t work for me, I started researching other options and working with labs and chemists in the hair-care industry. That ultimately led to the development of Pete & Pedro Boost Hair Growth Oil, which I use to support a healthy, hydrated scalp. I also realized I wanted a shampoo designed specifically for thinning hair and scalp health, which led us to develop DHT Defense Shampoo with ingredients including saw palmetto, pumpkin seed, pygeum, rosemary, caffeine, biotin, and niacin. These products became part of my routine because I wanted options beyond finasteride and minoxidil.

But products are only part of the equation. I also got serious about scalp health. I use a shampoo brush to gently massage and clean my scalp, helping remove oil, dead skin, styling-product buildup, and other junk. And after shampooing, I always use a hair conditioner. Shampoo and conditioner perform two different jobs, which is exactly why I’m not a fan of 2-in-1 products. Shampoo cleans; conditioner replenishes, smooths, and strengthens hair. I also don't use cheap, low-quality hair products, and I treat my hair like something worth protecting. I switched to a silk pillowcase because it pulls and tugs less on my hair while I sleep, and I added a hair supplement to my routine. I personally use Nutrafol. It’s definitely not cheap, but I’m willing to invest in taking care of my hair.

The biggest takeaway from my experience is simple: take action early. I caught my thinning when my hairline was just beginning to change, and instead of ignoring it and hoping for the best, I did something about it. You have multiple options—from improving your hair and scalp routine to medications and, for guys who need or want it, hair transplantation. The right solution will be different for everybody. At the end of the day, your hair is your responsibility. If keeping it matters to you, educate yourself, pay attention to changes, and start taking care of it before you’re staring at a bunch of hair in the drain wondering what the hell happened. I was genetically dealt a pretty crappy hand when it comes to hair loss, but I decided I wasn’t going to sit around and do nothing. It's your hair and your responsibility, so take action asap.

The supplement industry would love for you to believe you need a cabinet full of powders, pills, and potions to build an amazing body. You don’t. I’ve been working out for over 30 years; I used to own nutrition stores, and I’ve tried just about every natural supplement imaginable. What I’ve learned is that supplements can absolutely help—but they’re there to supplement the work, not replace it. If your diet sucks, you’re not training consistently, you’re sleeping like crap, and you’re not taking care of yourself, save your money.

No supplement can outwork a bad lifestyle. Get your ass in the gym, eat right, sleep, hydrate, and be consistent. Then, once you've got those fundamentals handled, supplements can help you get a little more out of the work you're already doing. And most importantly, do your own research and figure out what actually makes sense for you. That said, a handful of supplements are worth the money if you’re trying to build muscle, get leaner, improve performance, support healthy hormone levels, and ultimately build a better body.

Protein powder is at the top of my list because getting enough protein every day can be tough, especially if you’re trying to build or preserve muscle. I personally shoot for around one gram of protein per pound of body weight, and protein powder makes hitting that target quick and convenient. But remember—it's a supplement to real food, not a replacement.

I’m also a big believer in omega-3 fatty acids. Your body and brain need healthy fats, and getting enough omega-3s while cutting back on crappy fats can be an important part of a healthy diet.

Another supplement I use is psyllium husk, a source of soluble fiber. For me, it has helped with cholesterol, and because fiber helps keep you feeling full, it can also make staying within your calorie target easier.

For hormone support, I take a testosterone-support formula. My testosterone was 833 the last time I had it checked, but I’m not claiming a supplement caused that number. I simply like the ingredients and have been taking the product for over a year. This is also where supplement quality matters—you need to know and trust the company making what you're putting into your body.

Then there’s creatine, which I think is one of the biggest no-brainers for guys who train. I started taking it consistently about a year ago, and I currently use a creatine product that also includes MBP for bone-health support. Building a better body as we get older isn’t simply about looking muscular—it’s about staying strong, capable, and healthy for as many years as possible.

I’ve also been experimenting with Peak ATP to support workout energy and performance.

For workout energy, I keep things incredibly simple: caffeine. I love black coffee before training because it gives me energy without needing some crazy pre-workout. But you need to use caffeine responsibly. More isn’t better, especially if you're getting anxious, jittery, or screwing up your sleep.

Another one I love is citrulline because it supports nitric oxide production and blood flow. For workouts, that means better pumps and vascularity—which, come on, is freaking awesome when you're lean.

I also group vitamin D, zinc, and magnesium together because they’re important micronutrients involved in things like hormone regulation, immune function, and overall health.

Last is L-carnitine, which I’ve taken for years and like when I’m trying to get lean, especially with fasted cardio. But once again, none of these supplements magically burn fat, build muscle, or give you an amazing body while you sit on the couch. The foundation is always training, nutrition, sleep, hydration, and consistency.

items.text:
The ultimate Toronto Chinese food tour with https://www.youtube.com/@InstaNoodls — 4 stops, from decades-old Cantonese BBQ in Chinatown to fiery chili oil noodles in North York, ending at Canada's FIRST Hakka Chinese restaurant!

Toronto is home to one of the largest Chinese communities outside of Asia, but most people don't realize how vastly different each neighborhood eats. Joined by Toronto food insider Clement Leung, we're going on a fast-paced 40-minute food marathon to uncover dishes you can't even find in China. We start with crisp Cantonese barbecue and legendary roast meats at New Hong Fatt B.B.Q., taste handmade Northern-style dumplings rolled right by the front door at Yummy Yummy Dumplings, brave a bowl of fiery bowl-seared chili oil noodles at 7 Noodles in North York, and finish at Yueh Tung, Canada's historic first Hakka restaurant, where two sisters are preserving their family's legendary recipe for Indian-Chinese chili chicken!

items.title: The One FOOD Afghanistan Is Obsessed With!! (Kabuli Pulao)
items.summary: Kabuli Pulao — the national dish of Afghanistan! Today in Kabul we're watching Afghanistan's most famous dish made from start to finish, plus chopan lamb
items.text:
Kabuli Pulao — the national dish of Afghanistan! Today in Kabul we're watching Afghanistan's most famous dish made from start to finish, plus chopan lamb kebabs, hand-churned Afghan ice cream, and the original Afghan burger.

Afghan food is one of the most underrated cuisines in the world, and today my friend Bilal Kamal is taking me to eat some of the best of it in Kabul, Afghanistan. The main event is Kabuli Pulao — mountain-sized rice cooked with tender lamb, sweet carrots, and raisins — and at Abid Pulao Restaurant we see the entire process from start to finish before digging in. Then we try an original Afghan fast food: the Afghan burger at Osman Burger, a flatbread stuffed with fries, salad, and chutney. We cool down with Sheer Yakh at Ghazna Ice Cream — Afghan ice cream hand-churned for 2 hours — and finish with what I'd been waiting for all day: sizzling bone-in chopan lamb kebabs at a Turkmen restaurant!

0:41 How Kabuli Pulao is made at Abid Pulao Restaurant
